title: The Weekly: The Binance Hack and What Comes Next
text: NOV 2, 2026 The $6.3bn Binance exploit was the largest crypto hack on record, but its market impact has been far more contained than the headlines suggest. With $2.8bn frozen by Circle and Tether and 95% of affected funds replenished, the response shows how far on-chain infrastructure has matured. This week we look at how crypto beta and alts held up against US tech, why Bitcoin is likely to trade between its 50-week MA and $80k, and how the largest hedge fund de-risking in a decade, falling US 10-year yields and the US midterms could set up renewed risk appetite. Last week’s $6.3bn Binance exploit was the largest crypto hack on record, but we think the headline figure materially overstates the damage. Approximately $2.8bn in stolen assets were rapidly frozen by Circle , Tether and other issuers, while Binance has reportedly replenished 95% of affected funds through its own reserves and insurance fund. The speed of the response demonstrates how the industry’s capabilities have matured, with transparent onchain infrastructure enabling stolen assets to be frozen and traced, materially containing the damage. For perspective, the exploit represented just 3.7% of Binance’s $171bn in customer assets, with the ultimate economic loss considerably smaller. More importantly, Sunday’s $3.6bn in net withdrawals represented just 2.1% of customer assets, suggesting that even the largest hack in crypto history has failed to trigger a meaningful run on the exchange. Beyond traditional crypto markets, three emerging areas are seeing accelerating adoption: AI inference, tokenised collectibles and pre-IPO trading. Each demonstrates how blockchain infrastructure is expanding access to new and existing markets. AI token consumption continues to accelerate, creating demand for infrastructure that connects users with cheaper inference capacity. For example, Dolphin.ai operates a marketplace where users can access AI models from competing providers. Inference exchanges such as Surplus take this further, allowing suppliers to compete to fulfil inference requests, routing demand towards lower-cost capacity while improving supplier utilisation. As AI adoption scales, these marketplaces and exchanges are making inference cheaper and more accessible, creating a growing market for the infrastructure connecting supply and demand. On-chain trading card spending has accelerated, with weekly volumes approaching $100 million , compared with less than $20 million at the start of the year. Pokémon’s 30th anniversary has supported renewed interest, while integrations across Pump.fun , Jupiter and other Solana applications have expanded distribution. These platforms combine familiar collectibles with crypto-native mechanics: instant pack openings, verifiable ownership and immediate liquidity through stablecoin buybacks. title: The Weekly: Markets Are Refusing to Break
text: OCT 19, 2026 Crypto markets are refusing to break. Sentiment has fallen to Extreme Fear even though total crypto market cap is only 7% below its September peak, and crypto outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by more than 2% last week. Looking ahead, we cover China’s Q3 GDP beat, hyperscaler earnings and the 3 November US midterms as possible catalysts into year-end, plus this week’s DeFi yields across Aave, Maple, Pendle, Ethena and Lido. We cover: Why Bitcoin is absorbing negative macro headlines The growing disconnect between sentiment and price What could drive the next leg higher into year-end Crypto markets are refusing to break, finding clear support above $80k, around early September highs. Global crypto market capitalisation index ($; daily). Markets have had plenty of reasons to sell over the past two weeks. Brent crude surged towards $105, US CPI and PPI surprised to the upside, and concerns over AI financing intensified following CoreWeave’s sell-off. Each would ordinarily weigh on risk assets through higher inflation, tighter monetary policy or weaker growth expectations. Yet Bitcoin has repeatedly found buyers around $80,000, with little sustained downside despite these headwinds. BTC/USD. Bitcoin holds firm despite negative macro headlines. This is particularly constructive following Bitcoin’s breaks below its 200-day and 50-week moving averages, both traditionally bearish momentum signals. When negative news and bearish technicals fail to push prices materially lower, it suggests sellers are becoming exhausted. This is characteristic of bull market behaviour. Nasdaq futures are also up >1% this morning, with AI stocks rebounding strongly and further evidence that sellers are struggling to sustain downside momentum. The disconnect between sentiment and price is becoming increasingly pronounced. Since sentiment peaked on 21 September, total crypto market capitalisation has declined just 7%, while Fear & Greed has fallen 38% on an indexed basis. On 4 October, market capitalisation had returned to its September peak, yet sentiment was already 11% lower.
